chunks: And any one who changes the will, having heard it, shall be guilty and accountable; for God hears all and knows everything.
ai.seo_question: Who bears the sin for changing a divine matter after hearing it?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is frequently applied to the alteration of the divine covenant by the Ahl al-Bayt's contemporaries or the corruption of religious knowledge by scholars, highlighting that the sin lies with the active distorters. It underscores the divine attribute of 'Al-Sami' (The All-Hearing) regarding the precise words changed and 'Al-'Alim' (The All-Knowing) regarding the intent behind the alteration. This reinforces the concept of 'Ismah' (infallibility) of the Imams, as they preserve the unaltered truth against those who modify it for worldly gain.
